newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to VUB bank shares push SAX index up 0.23pts.
newsitem.headline: Gains to VUB bank shares push SAX index up 0.23pts.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares close mixed in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with gains to shares of bank VUB pushing the SAX index up 0.23 points to 208.91
VUB, Slovakia's largest commercial bank, gained 50 crowns to close at 1,830, with its average price - used for calculating the index - up 2.58 percent.

Oil and gas storage Nafta ked the day's activity, with 18,359 shares matched, closing down 30 at 2,000 -- but with an average price gain of 0.15 percent -- prompting brokers to say the figure appeared to have been a previously settled trade.
The two most heavily-capitalised issues on the market, oil refiner Slovnaft and steel maker VSZ, did not trade on Monday.

"There are some offers to sell Slovnaft share for a price more or less corresponding to current levels - around 950 crowns - but the volume (up to 3,000 shares) is not attractive enough," said Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt.

Overall volume decreased to 875,221 shares on Monday, of which the largest amount (854,781 shares) were the direct deals, from 3,246,301 shares traded on Friday. Turnover fell to 374.69 million crowns, from 1,271.67 million on Friday.
